title: Stop Repeating Yourself
story: The same print line is copy-pasted three times. When the format changes, someone will forget one copy.
goal: Keep the output the same, but define a function and call it for each item.
starter:
print("Samosa: " + str(10))
print("Tea: " + str(15))
print("Laddu: " + str(25))
hints: Whatever repeats becomes a function. What changes between the lines?
The name and the price change. Make them parameters.

def show(name, price):
    print(name + ": " + str(price))


show("Samosa", 10)
show("Tea", 15)
show("Laddu", 25)
socratic: Which parts of the three lines differ?
How many times would you edit the format after this?
Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what is the key idea in “Stop Repeating Yourself”?
solution:
def show(name, price):
    print(name + ": " + str(price))


show("Samosa", 10)
show("Tea", 15)
show("Laddu", 25)

clean.label: Fit it in 5 lines of code or fewer
